methods.name: Deauth and Disassociation
methods.description: Deauth ends authentication. Disassociation ends an AP link. Both also occur in normal use.
methods.advice: Check AP restart logs. Check PMF support on the AP and clients. PMF protects selected management frames. It does not stop all radio loss.
methods.limit: One disconnect is not an attack. AP work can also cause a burst.

methods.name: Directed Probe activity
methods.description: Probe Requests ask for Wi-Fi networks. Normal phones also send them.
methods.advice: Check the listed Probe Requests. Do not block a device from this observation alone.
methods.limit: A passive receiver sends no frames. MAC rotation does not prove one device.

methods.name: Evil Twin indicators
methods.description: An AP can copy a network name. A name match alone is not proof.
methods.advice: Check the BSSID and security on your router. Remove wrong saved network profiles after this check.
methods.limit: A guest AP can use the same name. A clone with the same security can pass this check.

methods.name: AP security policy change
methods.description: An AP security setting can change. GTH can compare saved policy with observed fields.
methods.advice: Check the router security policy. Confirm the BSSID and the intended PMF and AKM settings.
methods.limit: A real admin change can match this rule. A BSSID is not an AP identity proof.

methods.name: Multi-SSID response indicators
methods.description: Some AP tools answer requests for many network names.
methods.advice: Check the responding BSSID. Review saved Wi-Fi profiles and auto-connect settings.
methods.limit: The source uses an active challenge. Passive GTH does not send that challenge.

methods.name: EAPOL retry indicators
methods.description: Repeated WPA attempts can use different M2 nonces.
methods.advice: Check AP authentication logs. Check the client password. Use a strong Wi-Fi password.
methods.limit: A bad saved password or missing capture frames can match. Offline password tests are not visible.

methods.name: Authentication failure indicators
methods.description: An AP can return a failure status during authentication.
methods.advice: Check AP logs and client settings before changing access rules.
methods.limit: Failure frames do not show intent or a password.

methods.name: Association rejection indicators
methods.description: An AP can reject an Association or Reassociation request.
methods.advice: Check AP client limits and access settings. Compare the reject status with AP logs.
methods.limit: AP limits and client settings can cause rejects.

methods.name: WPS failure indicators
methods.description: WPS messages contain message types, nonces, and Config Error values.
methods.advice: Turn off WPS if it is not needed. Check AP WPS logs.
methods.limit: Normal setup retries can fail. A WPS message does not expose a PIN guess.
